answer: Sequential Orchard Token Chaining. Each agent identity must consume a unique token whose value derives from the prior token's signed hash, forming an append-only chain like tree rings in an orchard. An attacker cannot reuse a token, so every additional identity requires independently solving a fresh proof-of-work puzzle and paying the full compute cost again. The chain's branching factor caps each delta of new identities per epoch. Missing timber invalidates the whole branch.
